subject: math

objective.text: Measure two lengths and find how much longer or shorter one is. Use inches, feet and yards.

explanations.title: Find the difference
explanations.text: To compare two lengths, measure both. Then subtract the smaller length from the bigger length. The answer is how much longer one is.

explanations.title: Add on to find the difference
explanations.text: You can add on from the shorter length to the longer length. 17 plus 3 is 20. 20 plus 12 is 32. 3 plus 12 is 15.

explanations.title: Pick a tool and a unit
explanations.text: A yardstick can measure in inches, feet or yards. Use inches for short things. Use feet for longer things. Use yards for very long things.

explanations.title: Between two marks
explanations.text: If a length is between two marks, look at which mark is closer. More than halfway, say the next number. Less than halfway, say the smaller number.

explanations.title: Unit size changes the difference
explanations.text: The string and wall do not change. Feet are smaller than yards. We need more feet than yards to cover the same length.

examples.title: Paper and desk
examples.text: The desktop is 24 inches. The paper is 30 inches. The paper is longer. 30 minus 24 is 6. The paper is 6 inches longer.

examples.title: String and wall
examples.text: The string is 17 feet. The wall is 32 feet. 32 minus 17 is 15. You need 15 more feet of string. In yards, the difference is 5 yards.
